lectures.title: The President: position, election, term and removal

items: **Article 52:** There shall be a President of India.
**Article 53:** Executive power of the Union is vested in the President (exercised either directly or through officers subordinate to him).
**Nominal / Constitutional Head of the State:** the real executive is the Council of Ministers headed by the Prime Minister.
**First Citizen of India** and symbol of unity, integrity and solidarity of the nation.
President is **Head of the State**, not Head of the Government. Prime Minister = Head of the Government.

**Indirect election** by an Electoral College; the President is not directly elected.
**Elected members of both Houses of Parliament**
**Elected members of the Legislative Assemblies of the States**
**Elected members of the Legislative Assemblies of the Union Territories of Delhi and Puducherry**
**Who cannot vote:** Nominated members of Parliament and State Legislative Councils do not participate; nominated MPs/MLAs CANNOT vote; MLCs CANNOT vote.
**System:** Proportional Representation by means of Single Transferable Vote + Secret Ballot (Indirect; PR + STV).
**Value of vote:** value of vote of MLA and MP is calculated to ensure uniformity among states and parity between Union and States.
**Vote Value:** MLA vote value varies from State to State based on population ratios; MP vote value is uniform across all MPs.
**Disputes** regarding election are decided by the Supreme Court (final).
**Vacancy in Electoral College:** a Presidential election cannot be challenged or delayed on the grounds that vacancies exist in the electoral college (Art. 71(4)).
**President vs Vice-President:** President = Elected MPs + Elected MLAs (Legislative Councils excluded); Vice-President = ALL MPs (Elected + Nominated) (State Legislatures completely excluded).
**3.** Qualified for election as a member of the Lok Sabha.
**4.** Does not hold any office of profit.
President of India; Vice-President of India; Governor of a State
Constitutional Executive Heads; highest entry age required in the Indian Constitution.
**The 35-Year Executive Trio:** President (Art. 58) + Vice-President (Art. 66) + Governor (Art. 157) all share the exact same minimum age qualification of 35 years.
**Oath (Article 60):** administered by the Chief Justice of India (CJI) (or senior-most SC Judge).
**Re-election:** eligible for re-election any number of times (Art. 57).
**Resignation:** addressed to the Vice-President of India (communicated to LS Speaker).
**President:** Oath by CJI ↔ Resigns to Vice-President (Art. 56(1)(a)).
**Ground:** can be removed by Impeachment for violation of the Constitution (Art. 61).
**Charge** can be preferred by either House.
**Majority:** Special majority required in both Houses; impeachment by Parliament needs 2/3rd total membership.
**14 Days:** prior notice for President's Impeachment (Art. 61); impeachment notice requires ≥1/4th members' signatures.
**14-Day Cluster:** always associate 14 Days with President's Impeachment Notice (Art. 61).
**State Assemblies:** only elected members of State Assemblies do not participate in impeachment (they do vote in election).
**Vacancy:** in case of death, resignation, removal or otherwise → Vice-President acts as President (Art. 65).
**If both offices vacant:** Chief Justice of India (or senior-most Judge of SC) acts as President (President (Discharge of Functions) Act).

**Filling Presidential vacancy (Art. 62(2)):** a vacancy in the office of the President caused by death, resignation, or removal must be filled within 6 months (Vice-President acts as President in the interim).
Consolidated Fund of India (CFI); pension also from the Consolidated Fund of India
**Emoluments charged on:** Consolidated Fund of India.

lectures.title: Powers of the President: veto, pardon and ordinances

items: **Appoints:** Prime Minister, other Ministers, Governors, Judges of SC & HC, CAG, Attorney General, UPSC Chairman & members, Election Commissioners, Finance Commission, etc.
**Appoints the Prime Minister** (normally leader of majority party).
**Art. 78:** can seek information from the Prime Minister.
**Assents to Bills** (Art. 111): Absolute Veto, Suspensive Veto, Pocket Veto.
**Return of a Bill:** can return a Bill only once (except Money Bill).
**Promulgates Ordinances** when Parliament is not in session (Art. 123).

parts.t: Judicial, emergency, military and diplomatic powers
items: **Appoints Judges** of Supreme Court and High Courts.
**Art. 72:** power to grant pardons, reprieves, respites, remissions, suspend or commute sentences.
**Art. 143:** can seek advisory opinion of Supreme Court – not binding.
**Declares war and concludes peace** (on advice of CoM).
**Hung Parliament:** appointment of Prime Minister in case of hung Parliament.
**Dismissal** of government that has lost majority.
**Returning advice** of Council of Ministers for reconsideration (once – 44th Amendment): President can return advice once (44th CAA, 1978); bound thereafter.
Completely absorbs and removes both the sentence and conviction, placing the offender in the same position as if the offense had never been committed.
Substitutes a heavier form of punishment with a lighter form (e.g., Death sentence -- Rigorous Life Imprisonment).
Reduces the period/duration of the sentence without changing its fundamental character (e.g., 2 years rigorous imprisonment -- 1 year rigorous imprisonment).
Awards a lesser sentence in place of the original penalty due to special personal circumstances (e.g., pregnancy, mental/physical disability).
Grants a temporary stay or postponement of the execution of a sentence (especially death penalty) to allow time to seek Presidential pardon.
**Constitutional Framework:** governed under Article 123 (President of India) and Article 213 (Governor of a State).
**Nature of Power:** the ordinance-making power is a legislative power of the Executive, NOT an executive or administrative function.
**Core Pre-Condition:** promulgated only when the Legislature is in recess (except when both Houses are in session in a bicameral legislature, or the single House in unicameral states).
**Satisfaction:** the Head of State is satisfied that circumstances exist requiring immediate action.
**Co-extensive Scope:** an Ordinance has the same force, effect, and limitations as an Act of Parliament / State Legislature.
**Co-extensive:** ordinance-making power is co-extensive with legislative power of Parliament.

parts.t: What an ordinance can and cannot do
items: Can amend, modify, or repeal any existing Central/State legislation within competence.
Can be given retrospective operation from an earlier date like an ordinary statute.
Can introduce or amend tax provisions within legislative power.
Cannot be used to amend the Constitution under Article 368 (Limited to ordinary legislative power).
Subject to Article 13(2); void if it takes away or abridges Part III rights.
Cannot be issued when both Houses are in active session.

parts.t: The six-week rule, withdrawal and judicial review
items: **Reassembly Rule:** an Ordinance must be laid before Parliament/State Legislature when it reassembles and ceases to operate 6 weeks after the date of reassembly unless approved earlier.
**Different Assembly Dates:** if the two Houses reassemble on different dates, the 6-week countdown begins from the later of the two dates.
**Maximum Lifespan:** maximum gap between sessions (6 months under Art. 85/174) + Parliamentary approval window (6 weeks) = 6 Months and 6 Weeks.
**Withdrawal Absolute Authority:** any option stating "The President cannot repeal or withdraw an Ordinance once issued" → FALSE (can withdraw anytime under Art. 123(2)(b)).
**Judicial Review Status:** ordinance-making power is NOT beyond judicial review.
**D.C. Wadhwa (1987) & Krishna Kumar Singh (2017):** Re-promulgation of ordinances without legislative ratification is a subversion of the Constitution.
**Article 63:** There shall be a Vice-President of India.
**Second-highest constitutional office** (next to the President in the Order of Precedence).
**Ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha** (Art. 64), but not a member of RS.
**Not a member:** Vice-President is not a member of either House of Parliament.
**Not appointed** by the President (he is elected).
**Indirect election** by an Electoral College consisting of members of both Houses of Parliament (elected + nominated): ALL MPs of both Houses.
**State Legislative Assemblies do NOT participate** (major difference from Presidential election); State MLAs/MLCs have NO role.
**Method:** Proportional Representation by means of Single Transferable Vote + Secret Ballot (Indirect; PR + STV).
**Disputes:** all doubts and disputes regarding election decided by the Supreme Court (Art. 71) – decision is final.
**Nominated MPs** do vote in Vice-Presidential election.
**State MLAs** do not vote in Vice-Presidential election.
**3.** Qualified for election as a member of the Rajya Sabha.
**4.** Does not hold any office of profit.
**Oath (Article 69):** administered by the President of India.
**Re-election:** eligible for re-election any number of times.
**Resignation:** addressed to the President of India.
**Removal (Art. 67(b)):** by a resolution of the Rajya Sabha passed by a majority of all the then members of the Council (Effective Majority) and agreed to by the Lok Sabha.
**No formal impeachment** like the President; 14 days’ notice required.
**Presides** over the sittings of Rajya Sabha.
**Casting vote:** has a casting vote in case of a tie.
**Does not preside** when a resolution for his removal is under consideration.
**Vacancy:** when the office of President falls vacant due to death, resignation, removal or otherwise.
**Inability:** when the President is unable to discharge his functions (absence, illness, etc.).
**Maximum period as Acting President:** 6 months (election for new President must be held within 6 months).
**Salary:** draws salary and allowances as Chairman of Rajya Sabha (not charged on the Consolidated Fund of India as Vice-President).
**When acting as President** → entitled to salary, allowances and privileges of the President.
**"Who is NOT Charged on CFI?" Elimination Trio – Vice-President:** draws salary solely as the Chairman of the Council of States (Rajya Sabha); the office of VP carries no separate charged salary.
Resolution by Rajya Sabha + agreement of Lok Sabha
**Two full terms as Vice-President:** served only by Dr. S. Radhakrishnan and Mohammad Hamid Ansari.

lectures.title: The Prime Minister and the Union Council of Ministers

items: **Real Executive Head of the Union** (President is the nominal/constitutional head).
**Leader** of the majority party/coalition in the Lok Sabha.
**Head of the Government:** President = Head of the State; Prime Minister = Head of the Government.
Council of Ministers with the Prime Minister at the head to aid and advise the President
Other provisions as to Ministers (appointment, tenure, responsibility, etc.)
**Normally** the leader of the majority party in Lok Sabha.
**House:** can be from Lok Sabha or Rajya Sabha.
**Need not be a member of Parliament** at the time of appointment (must become member within 6 months – Art. 75(5)).
**Only PM who was never an MP when appointed:** (Conventionally rare; must get elected within 6 months).
**PM can be a member of Rajya Sabha** (e.g., Indira Gandhi initially, Manmohan Singh).
**Indira Gandhi** was the first Prime Minister who was a Rajya Sabha member at the time of appointment.
**Oath of PM:** administered by the President.
**Responsibility:** PM is not responsible to Rajya Sabha (only to Lok Sabha).

parts.t: Powers and functions of the Prime Minister
items: **1. Head of Council of Ministers:** selects, allocates portfolios, can ask any minister to resign.

**2. Link between President and Council of Ministers (Art. 78):** communicates all decisions of CoM to the President; furnishes information required by the President; submits matters for reconsideration of CoM if President so requires.

**Prime Minister's Duties (Art. 78):** PM communicates all decisions and administrative proposals to the President and submits any matter decided by an individual minister for Council consideration if required by the President.
**3. Leader of the Lok Sabha** (Leader of the House).
**5. Chairman of important bodies:** NITI Aayog (earlier Planning Commission); National Development Council; National Integration Council; Inter-State Council; National Disaster Management Authority.
**6. Advises the President on:** appointment of other Ministers; summoning & prorogation of Parliament; dissolution of Lok Sabha; Declaration of Emergency (recommendation of Cabinet).
First Prime Minister of independent India; longest serving
Indian History #105; Indian Polity #7; Indian Society #1
**Deputy Prime Minister:** not a constitutional post (only political).

**Deputy Prime Minister Post:** an extra-constitutional / non-constitutional post created for political convenience; carries the status of a Cabinet Minister without superior prime-ministerial powers.
**First Deputy Prime Minister:** Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel, 1947–1950.

parts.t: Union Ministers: framework, appointment and oath
items: **The term "Council"** in Indian Polity spans three distinct constitutional institutions; Council of Ministers (Union & State): Executive body aiding and advising the President/Governor.
**Constitutional Framework:** governed under Part V (Articles 74, 75, 77, 78); the Council of Ministers with the Prime Minister at the head aids and advises the President of India.
**Appointment (Art. 75(1)):** Prime Minister is appointed by the President; other Union Ministers are appointed by the President on the advice of the Prime Minister.
**Tenure (Art. 75(2)):** Ministers hold office during the pleasure of the President (Trap: legally holds office during the pleasure of the President, NOT the Prime Minister).
**Pleasure of Office:** Ministers hold office during the pleasure of the President / Governor, NOT the pleasure of the Prime Minister / Chief Minister.
**Oath:** the President administers both the Oath of Office and Oath of Secrecy under the Third Schedule.
President of India (Ministers route via PM)
**Removal Method & Authority:** dismissed by President on PM's advice / loss of Lok Sabha majority.
**House Membership:** a Union Minister can be a member of either Lok Sabha or Rajya Sabha (no requirement to be a Lok Sabha member).

**Non-Member Ministers:** a person who is not a member of either House can be appointed as a Minister, but must become a member within 6 consecutive months; otherwise, ceases to be a Minister (Art. 75(5)).
**Right to speak (Art. 88):** right to speak and participate in proceedings of both Houses & Joint Sittings -- YES.
**Right to vote (Art. 88 Trap):** right to vote in the House of which the Minister is NOT a member -- NO (can vote ONLY in the House where they hold membership).
**Collective Responsibility (Art. 75(3)):** Council of Ministers (including PM) is collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha.
**Principle:** the Council of Ministers is collectively answerable to the popular House (Lok Sabha); all ministers sink or swim together.
**No-Confidence Motion:** if a No-Confidence Motion is passed → entire Council (including PM) must resign.
**Loss of majority:** if the government loses a vote of confidence/majority in Lok Sabha, the entire Council must resign ("Sink or swim together").
**Confidence Motion:** moved on the floor by the Council of Ministers/Government to demonstrate majority.
**Individual Responsibility:** Ministers are answerable to Parliament for administrative/bureaucratic lapses under their respective portfolios.

**Collective Responsibility Trap:** Ministers are collectively responsible ONLY to the Lower House (Art. 75(3) to Lok Sabha; Art. 164(2) to Legislative Assembly) — NOT to the Rajya Sabha, Parliament as a whole, or the President/Governor.

parts.t: Size of the Council of Ministers
items: **91st Constitutional Amendment Act, 2003:** total Ministers (including PM) shall not exceed 15% of the total strength of Lok Sabha.
**15% Ceiling Limit (91st CAA, 2003) – Union (Art. 75(1A)):** total number of Union Ministers, including the PM, cannot exceed 15% of the total strength of the Lok Sabha.
**States:** same limit applies to States (including CM).
